$comment: X-34 RULE-OWNERSHIP INVENTORY (single source of truth). Each rule family has exactly ONE normative owner document; other documents carry only informative summaries that reference the owner. scripts/rule_ownership.py (make rule-ownership) and tests/test_rule_ownership.py enforce: the owner states the rule, no non-owner document carries a BARE normative restatement, and the I-D's deployment-defined-interface count matches the bullets it lists. docs/rule-ownership.md is generated from this file. Registry / well-known ownership layering is deferred to X-25 (Batch 4) and deliberately NOT covered here.

families.title: Intermediaries (MSP / Delivery Service / RDP) never access plaintext
families.owner_anchor: Object model, Delivery-Service mapping, and Security Considerations

informative_refs.note: §7.3 actor list and the §9 privacy summary describe the property and defer to the I-D
ICS row 051 (Evidence carries no plaintext) tagged [I-D]

families.note: An E2EE property, not a sample-checkable LINT rule; owned by the wire/security document.

families.title: KeyPackages are single-use; the MSP removes a consumed KeyPackage and rejects reuse

informative_refs.note: ICS rows 024 and 149 tagged [I-D] (single-use / pool integrity)

the Deployment-Defined-Interfaces Delivery-Service bullet adds the DISTINCT pool-integrity rule (idempotent reserve->commit, per-peer quota) and explicitly complements {{keypackage-rules}}; the T4 Security-Considerations mention is an in-document analytical echo

families.note: The reserve->commit pool-integrity rule is a distinct, complementary I-D-owned requirement, not a restatement of single-use.

families.title: The availability delivery grade is declared per content class in the signed BW-ORG and is never implicit or default

informative_refs.note: the delivery-state model owns the DISTINCT anchoring rule: availability anchors at authenticated S2 -> event D.1-ContentConsignment
clause 6 owns the DISTINCT legal-effect rule (Article 44(1)(c) gating); ICS row 113 (GRD-1) indexes the declaration rule to [UMB]

families.note: Not one rule in three documents but three ASPECTS with three owners: declaration (umbrella §8.3b), state anchoring (I-D), legal effect (TS clause 6). The inventory records the decomposition that resolves the apparent duplication.

families.title: Federation registries (reason codes, content classes) are owned by the design authority under umbrella §13.4, as machine-readable artefacts

informative_refs.note: the I-D defines the FIELDS, the lexical value spaces and the unknown-code ingest rule only (IANA Considerations, X-25 registry layering); registry contents/governance are not restated
clause 8.1/8.3 owns the ERD event mappings the registered reasons bind to

families.note: X-25 / X-34 residual: the transport I-D previously claimed to BE the registry ('initially this document') and registered well-known resources defined elsewhere; the split gives each registry one owner and moves the well-known registration to umbrella §8.1.

families.title: RDP(in) is the sole evidence-authoritative acceptance-policy evaluator
families.owner_anchor: Acceptance-policy evaluation — the evaluator of record
families.owner_present: RDP\(in\) shall be the \*\*sole evidence-authoritative evaluator\*\*

informative_refs.note: §7.2 responsibility table and the §8.3 bullet describe the split and defer to the TS
the delivery-state model consumes the evaluated outcome; it does not evaluate

families.note: X-10: the former two-owner text (umbrella: the MSP evaluates; TS: RDP(in) evaluates) is collapsed to one owner. A prose-ownership family, not a sample-checkable LINT rule.

families.title: Legal-effect issuance is gated on the signed short-lived status assertion (D6)
families.owner_present: MUST NOT\*\* issue DE-v1 against a recipient UID unless it holds a \*\*valid \(unexpired\) signed status assertion

informative_refs.note: the delivery-state model consumes the gate; the hold note defers to the umbrella

families.note: D6 (F-10/X-07): one mechanism, two findings. The capability object is STATUS-v1; the EDD contract v1.8.0 serves it; LINT-DISC-25 checks it.

interfaces.note: The prose count of deployment-defined HTTP surfaces MUST equal the number of interface bullets in the section (the review found 'Two' while four are listed).
